# MedLens

> AI-powered clinical information intelligence. MedLens turns fragmented medical
> information (history, symptoms, allergies, medications, lab reports, prescriptions,
> prior records) into a structured, source-traceable, human-reviewable patient record.
> It organizes and summarizes information — it does NOT diagnose, prescribe, or
> recommend treatment.

## What MedLens does

- Extracts clinical values from uploaded reports through a validated pipeline
  (OCR/text → segment → structured extraction → schema validation → range check →
  provenance → conflict scan → human review).
- Computes reference-range status (Low / Within range / High / Unknown) using ONLY the
  range printed in the source report. It never invents a reference range; when a source
  omits one, it says "Reference range not provided in source."
- Attaches provenance to every fact (user-provided, document-extracted, AI-generated,
  human-verified) with a link to the exact span in the original document.
- Detects conflicts (e.g. two reports disagreeing on the same test) and surfaces them for
  a human — it never auto-resolves them.
- Describes trends as data only, never as clinical interpretation.
- Produces a safety-gated summary that is linted against diagnostic and prescriptive
  language before display.

## Key pages

- Dashboard (/): patient overview, attention items, recent labs, trends.
- Patient (/patient): demographics and history with per-field source labels.
- Reports (/reports): ingested documents and the split-screen document viewer.
- Review (/review): human-in-the-loop verification, conflict resolution, audit trail.
- Timeline & Trends (/timeline): chronology and data-only trend analysis.
- AI Summary (/summary): safety-gated, exportable information summary.

## Safety

MedLens is an information-organization tool, not a medical device or clinician. All
demo data is synthetic and fictional. Clinical decisions must be made by a qualified
healthcare professional.
